user.title: Share your energy data with Kilowattlas
user.description:
Kilowattlas is a public map of home energy production and an energy-sharing service. This integration sends the readings of the power sensors in your Energy dashboard to kilowattlas.com as soon as they are measured, and nothing else.

- Your home position is sent once as a suggestion; you confirm it on the website.
- Solar and battery are shown publicly on the map, at about 100 m precision, without your name. Grid, home and individual device power are visible only to you.
- You can change this per channel on kilowattlas.com, and stop at any time by removing this integration and deleting the installation on the website.

link.title: Approve the link
link.description:
Open this page, sign in and approve the link:

channels.title: Choose what to share
channels.description: These power sensors are set up in your Energy dashboard. Untick any you do not want to share. Sensors you add to the Energy dashboard later are shared too; you can change this here at any time, and switch each channel off on kilowattlas.com.

energy_missing.title: Set up the Energy dashboard
energy_missing.description: Kilowattlas shares the power sensors of your Energy dashboard, and none are set up yet. Add them under **Settings → Dashboards → Energy** (the power fields of grid, solar, battery, home and individual devices), then check again. Or enter the same sensors here.

menu_options.channels: I have set up the Energy dashboard, check again

manual.title: Enter your sensors
manual.description: The same power settings as the Energy dashboard. Fill in what you have; everything is optional, but at least one sensor is needed.

grid.name: Grid
grid.description: The power at your grid connection, as in the Energy dashboard's grid settings.

data_description.grid_mode: One sensor that is positive when you import from the grid; one sensor that is positive when you export (inverted); or two sensors, one for import and one for export.
data_description.grid_power: With two sensors: the power taken from the grid.
data_description.grid_power_to: Only with two sensors: the power returned to the grid.

solar.name: Solar
solar.description: The power your solar panels produce.

battery.name: Battery
battery.description: Your home battery, as in the Energy dashboard's battery settings.

data_description.battery_mode: One sensor that is positive when the battery discharges; one sensor that is positive when it charges (inverted); or two sensors, one for discharging and one for charging.
data_description.battery_power: With two sensors: the power out of the battery.
data_description.battery_power_to: Only with two sensors: the power into the battery.

home.name: Home
home.description: The power the whole home uses, as in the Energy dashboard's home settings.

data_description.home_power: Positive; measured at the main panel.

devices.name: Individual devices
devices.description: Devices you also track in the Energy dashboard, such as an EV charger or a heat pump.

data_description.device_power: One sensor per device; positive while it draws power.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-link Kilowattlas
reauth_confirm.description: Kilowattlas no longer accepts the link for this installation. Approve a new link on the website to continue sharing.

progress.wait_for_approval:

error.consent_required: You need to agree before the integration can share your readings.
error.invalid_power_config: With two sensors, choose both of them.

abort.expired: The linking code expired before it was approved. Start over to get a new code.

no_channels.title: Kilowattlas has nothing to share
no_channels.description: No power sensor is set up in your Energy dashboard. Add the power fields under **Settings → Dashboards → Energy**, or enter the sensors in the Kilowattlas options.

confirm.title: Share from your Energy dashboard
confirm.description: Your Energy dashboard now has power sensors set up. Kilowattlas can share those instead of the sensors entered in its own options, so you keep one list in one place. Your channels and their history on kilowattlas.com stay as they are.
